headline: Overseas Highway Access and Reef Protection
reservation: State park entry for John Pennekamp or Bahia Honda is separate from boat tour bookings, which often sell out weeks in advance. Individual island accommodations vary widely in policy; travelers must verify specific dockage or parking rules with their provider. Visit the official Florida State Parks website to check current capacity limits for beach access.

days.title: Upper Keys Ecosystems

stops.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
stops.detail: Explore the first undersea park in the U.S. via glass-bottom boat or guided snorkeling excursions.

stops.name: Dagny Johnson Key Largo Hammock Botanical State Park
stops.detail: Walk the paved trails through one of the largest remaining tracts of West Indian tropical hardwood hammock.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour of active driving time; traffic on US-1 varies significantly
days.note: Water visibility is highly dependent on wind speeds; check marine forecasts locally.

days.title: The Middle Keys Transit

stops.name: Sombrero Beach
stops.detail: Visit this public park in Marathon for coastal views and a chance to see a protected turtle nesting area.

stops.name: Old Seven Mile Bridge
stops.detail: Walk the refurbished section of the historic bridge for a unique perspective of the surrounding turquoise waters.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the transit to Marathon; bridge traffic can be slow
days.note: Ensure your vehicle has a full tank before crossing the longer bridge spans.

days.title: Lower Keys and Key West

stops.name: Bahia Honda State Park
stops.detail: View the iconic rusted remains of the Flagler Railroad Bridge from the white sand beaches.

stops.name: Fort Zachary Taylor Historic State Park
stops.detail: Explore the Civil War-era fortress and the park's beach, often cited for the best water clarity in Key West.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours including stops; Lower Keys speed limits are strictly enforced for deer protection
days.note: Key West is best explored on foot or bicycle once your vehicle is parked at your lodging.

intel.title: State Park Capacity
intel.text: Parks like Bahia Honda frequently reach capacity by mid-morning on weekends. Entry is not guaranteed once the 'Full' sign is posted at the gate.

intel.title: Key West Constraints
intel.text: Public parking in the historic district is extremely limited and managed by meters or residential permits. Utilize park-and-ride lots or lodging-provided spaces whenever possible.

intel.title: Strategic Refueling
intel.text: Fuel is readily available in Key Largo and Marathon, but stations are sparse on the long bridge sections. Expect higher costs at remote island marinas compared to the mainland.

intel.title: Marine Interference
intel.text: Standard cellular service is reliable along US-1, but can drop once you are several miles offshore for reef activities. Signal strength varies in the remote backcountry of the Lower Keys.

intel.title: Bridge Transit
intel.text: The Overseas Highway is a single-entry route; accidents can cause multi-hour delays. Allow significant buffers when traveling to Key West for timed flight departures.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at EYW or MIA; if arriving from Miami, stock up in Florida City before crossing the 18-mile stretch to Key Largo.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is ideal for the narrow streets of Key West; RVs face significant parking restrictions and limited turnaround points in the Lower Keys.
plan.goldenHour: Mallory Square is the traditional sunset gathering point in Key West, though seasonal clouds may obscure the horizon.
